content: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies, including to this drug or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness or reduced alertness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects, making you more dizzy or less alert. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages while taking this medication unless your doctor explicitly permits it. Drinking alcohol during treatment may lead to a rapid heartbeat and skin flushing. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using this medication, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable birth control methods with your doctor while using this medication and for one month after your last dose. If you become pregnant, contact your doctor immediately to discuss the risks and benefits of continuing this medication. The effects of this drug on human sperm are unknown, but based on animal studies, the manufacturer recommends waiting a period of time after completing treatment before attempting to father a child. It is also unclear if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use additional reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, your doctor may recommend lab tests, such as kidney or liver function tests and complete blood counts, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. To prevent reinfection and control the spread of fungal infections, ask your doctor or pharmacist for advice. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. This medication is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, hair, and nails that do not respond to topical treatments like creams or lotions. Treating these infections helps alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, peeling, scaly skin, and discolored nails. This medication works by inhibiting the growth of fungi. Shake the bottle well before each dose. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor. For optimal absorption, take it with or after a meal containing a moderate amount of fat. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also determined by weight. The duration of treatment depends on the type of infection being treated. It may take several weeks to months to complete treatment for infections of the scalp, feet, or body. Antifungal medications work best when the drug concentration in your body is maintained at a consistent level. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow the infection to return. Common side effects include headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach upset, tiredness, dizziness, or trouble sleeping. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor promptly. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare but seek immediate medical attention if it occurs. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance.
